Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

Along the coast of Bohol, fishing families once cut mangroves for firewood and cleared them to build fishponds. The loss seemed small at first, because the trees grew in muddy places that few people visited. When strong typhoons arrived, however, the difference became clear. Villages that had lost their mangroves often saw more homes damaged by storm surge, while villages behind thick stands of trees suffered less. Mangrove roots slow incoming waves and trap mud, so the shoreline wears away more slowly. The trees also shelter young fish and crabs, which later support the catch of the same families who once cut them down. Since the 1990s, several towns have replanted mangroves with help from schools and fisherfolk associations. Not every effort succeeded. Seedlings planted on sandy beaches or in the wrong tidal zone often died within months. The projects that lasted chose species suited to each site and planted where mangroves had grown before. They also asked residents to tend the young trees until they were established.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Mangrove roots slow incoming waves and trap mud, so coastlines behind them erode much more slowly.
Mangroves shield villages and fish stocks, and replanting lasts when it fits the site.
Typhoons striking Bohol have grown stronger and more frequent since the 1990s.
Forests of every kind protect Philippine communities from natural disasters.

reveal.terms: Main idea: the one statement that covers the whole passage, not just one part of it.
reveal.shortcut: Check each choice against the first half (what mangroves do) and the second half (replanting). Only the key covers both.
reveal.why_correct: It covers both halves of the passage: what mangroves do for villages, and what made replanting succeed.

why_wrong.o1: True, but it is one supporting detail; it leaves out the fishing benefit and the whole replanting story.
why_wrong.o3: The passage never compares the strength or number of typhoons over time.
why_wrong.o4: The passage is about mangroves on the Bohol coast, not all forests in the country.

items.stem:
Read the selection below, then answer the question.

Many sari-sari stores let regular customers buy on credit, writing each purchase in a small notebook called a listahan. For the store owner, this arrangement is both a service and a risk. It keeps neighbors loyal, because a family short of cash until payday can still buy rice, sardines and cooking oil. But unpaid balances tie up money the owner needs to restock the shelves, and a store with empty shelves soon loses even its cash customers. Aling Rosa, who has run a store in Marikina for twenty years, follows a simple rule. No customer gets new credit until the previous week's balance is paid, except during emergencies such as illness in the family. She writes the rule on a card taped beside the window where customers pay. At first, a few regular buyers took offense and went to another store down the street. Most of them came back within a month. Aling Rosa says the rule protects friendships as much as it protects her income. In her experience, small debts that pile up quietly are what make neighbors start avoiding each other.

According to the passage, when does Aling Rosa allow new credit before last week's balance is paid?

options.text: When a customer has bought from her for many years
Whenever her shelves are fully stocked
During emergencies such as illness in the family
Never, since her rule allows no exceptions

reveal.terms: Detail question: the answer is stated in the passage.
reveal.shortcut: Find the word "except" in the sentence that states her rule.
reveal.why_correct: The passage states this exception directly.

why_wrong.o1: Long-time customers get no special exception in the passage.
why_wrong.o2: Stock level is mentioned only as a reason credit is risky, not as an exception.
why_wrong.o4: The rule names one exception: emergencies.

items.stem:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

The rice terraces of Ifugao were carved into the mountainsides by hand over many generations. Each terrace depends on the ones above it. Water is led from the forest at the summit through channels and bamboo pipes, then flows down from field to field. Stone or earth walls hold each field in place, and a single break can send mud and water onto the terraces below. Because the system is shared, a family that neglects its walls can harm its neighbors. Repairs have long been treated as a communal duty rather than a private chore. The forest above the terraces matters just as much, since it holds the rain that feeds the channels during the dry months. In recent decades, many young people have left for jobs in the lowlands and abroad. Some terraces have collapsed for lack of hands to repair them. Local groups now pair elders with students during the planting season. They hope to pass on both the techniques and the sense of obligation that kept the terraces whole for centuries.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: The bamboo pipes and stone channels that carry water down the Ifugao terraces
The history of rice farming throughout the Philippines
Why young people from Ifugao prefer jobs abroad to jobs in the lowlands
Why the shared terraces need communal upkeep, and how that is now at risk

reveal.terms: Main idea: the point that the whole passage builds toward.
reveal.shortcut: Join the beginning (a shared system) to the end (who will keep it up).
reveal.why_correct: The passage explains why upkeep is shared, then why it is failing and what is being done.

why_wrong.o1: The water system is one part of the passage; the decline and the response are left out.
why_wrong.o2: The passage is about the Ifugao terraces only.
why_wrong.o3: The passage says they leave for both, and it never compares the two.

Read the selection below, then answer the question.

Dengue cases in the Philippines usually rise during the rainy months, from June to October. The virus is carried by the Aedes mosquito, which bites mostly during the day, especially in the early morning and late afternoon. Unlike many other mosquitoes, it breeds in clean, still water rather than in swamps or canals. Old tires, flower vases, uncovered drums and even bottle caps can hold enough water for its eggs. The eggs can survive for months on the dry wall of a container and hatch once rain fills it again. For this reason, health workers ask every household to follow a simple routine. Once a week, search the house and yard for containers that collect water, then empty, scrub, cover or throw them away. Scrubbing matters because emptying a container does not remove the eggs stuck to its sides. Spraying insecticide can kill adult mosquitoes, but it does little if breeding sites remain. A new generation soon replaces the ones that died.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of this passage on dengue?

options.text: Preventing dengue depends on clearing breeding water at home every week.
The Aedes mosquito bites mostly in the early morning and late afternoon.
Insecticide spraying is the most effective way to prevent dengue.
Mosquito-borne diseases are the leading health problem in the country.

reveal.terms: Main idea: the one statement that covers the whole passage.
reveal.shortcut: The passage builds toward the weekly routine; the facts about breeding explain why it works.
reveal.why_correct: The passage explains where the mosquito breeds and why the weekly search-and-scrub routine matters more than spraying.

why_wrong.o2: True, but it is one detail; the passage is about breeding sites and how to remove them.
why_wrong.o3: The passage says spraying does little while breeding sites remain.
why_wrong.o4: The passage makes no such comparison and covers only dengue.

PAGASA reports not only the air temperature but also the heat index, a measure of how hot the body feels once humidity is counted. The two numbers can differ by a wide margin. On a humid afternoon in Metro Manila, an air temperature of 33°C can produce a heat index above 40°C. At that level, the body struggles to cool itself, because moist air slows the evaporation of sweat from the skin. Sweat that does not evaporate carries away little heat, so body temperature keeps rising. Heat cramps, exhaustion and, in the worst cases, heat stroke can follow. Outdoor workers such as traffic enforcers, construction crews and street vendors face the greatest risk because they cannot easily move indoors. Some local governments have responded by shortening outdoor shifts at midday and setting up water stations along busy roads. Health officers say these steps work best when people also learn the early signs of heat illness, such as dizziness and headache. Reducing exposure during the hottest hours remains the simplest protection.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Street vendors in Metro Manila should work only at night.
High heat index readings endanger outdoor workers unless exposure is reduced.
Moist air slows the evaporation of sweat from the skin.
Hot weather is the greatest health danger facing people in the Philippines today.

reveal.terms: Main idea.
reveal.shortcut: Look for the statement that joins the definition at the start with the advice at the end.
reveal.why_correct: It joins the danger of a high heat index to the responses that reduce exposure, which together make up the passage.

why_wrong.o1: The passage recommends no such schedule.
why_wrong.o3: True, but it is one step in the explanation.
why_wrong.o4: The passage makes no comparison with other health dangers.

The Philippine eagle is one of the largest eagles in the world, and it is found nowhere else. A breeding pair needs a territory of thousands of hectares of forest to find enough prey, such as flying lemurs, monkeys and snakes. The female lays a single egg only once every two years. Both parents care for the young eagle for many months after it hatches, until it can hunt on its own.
